text:
**Short answer:** For a full day or more of backup, the **BLUETTI Elite 200 V2** is the pick from these results. If you only need to cover a short outage, a smaller unit will do.

**Why the Elite 200 V2**
- According to [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-keep-reptile-heat-on-in-a-power-outage), its 2,073.6 Wh LiFePO4 battery and 2,600 W output can run a 100 W ceramic heat emitter on a thermostat for about a day. It costs $899 and was listed in stock on 2026-11-04. [Buy link](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2). Dealectric says its code DEALECTRIC takes $44.95 off, and the link applies it already.
- Reptile heat is a small, steady load. Dealectric lists under-tank heat mats at 4–24 W, ceramic emitters at 50–150 W and deep heat projectors at 50–80 W. A thermostat also runs them only part of the time.
- A power station suits this better than a small battery backup. [Off Grid Power Boom](https://offgridpowerboom.com/reptile-heat-battery-backup/) says the watt-hour capacity is why: you need sustained watts for hours, not just a clean handoff. Its runtimes are arithmetic (Wh ÷ watts), not a tested overnight run.

**Other options from the same source ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-keep-reptile-heat-on-in-a-power-outage))**
- **BLUETTI AC180** (1,152 Wh): about 15–18 hours for a 100 W emitter on a thermostat. It's $449 in BLUETTI's cart and back in stock in late November.
- **BLUETTI Elite 30 V2** (288 Wh, $289.99): about 6–8 hours for a 24 W heat mat. This is the budget choice for a small setup.
- **EcoFlow DELTA 3** (1,024 Wh, 1,800 W): price and stock are on Amazon, and the results give no runtime for it.

**Caveats**
- Dealectric is the retailer selling these units, so treat its runtimes as estimates. They are calculations, not tests.
- A heat mat uses far less power than a lamp and lasts much longer. Insulating the enclosure first stretches the battery further. A Reddit user in [r/reptiles](https://www.reddit.com/r/reptiles/comments/1qahs27/we_had_to_get_creative_during_a_power_outage_and/) wrapped their terrariums in insulation, and another suggests keeping a large power bank ready.
- For backup that doesn't need power, [Petco](https://www.petco.com/pet-education/reptile/general/caring-for-your-reptile-during-a-power-outage) suggests chemical hand warmers and warm water bottles wrapped in towels. Don't feed your reptile until temperatures are back to normal. Sensitive species such as chameleons, along with hatchlings and sick animals, have much less margin, so call your vet if you see lethargy or labored breathing.

**Sizing tip:** Divide the station's watt-hours by your heater's average wattage. Choose your unit based on how long your outages usually last.
